findings.title: [P1] Canonicalize heredoc destinations before suppressing scanning
findings.body: The new classifier checks destination paths without resolving `..` components. Consequently, `tee .git/objects/../hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF'` is classified as writing ordinary data. A body containing `trap 'rm -rf / --no-preserve-root' EXIT` is then discarded because `trap` is neither an interpreter nor a destructive command in the classifier. If this overwrites an existing executable pre-commit hook, appending `git commit --allow-empty -m trigger` executes the destructive body within the same Bash invocation. The basename check misses this implicit hook execution. Canonicalize destinations before checking executable locations, and conservatively retain bodies when resolution is uncertain.

findings.description:
The new heredoc consumer classifier (on by default) stops scanning the body of a heredoc whose consumer is 'nonexec' (e.g. `cat <<'EOF' > x`) and keeps only segments whose first command word is a fence verb. The per-segment command-word extraction in _bdb_hd_segword drops destructive commands that are not the first word: `$(rm -rf ~)` and backtick forms (the `$(` fallback is skipped for quoted delimiters, line 582-584), `2>/dev/null rm -rf ~`, `x=$(rm -rf ~)` (assignment stripped, leaves `-rf`), and `if :; then rm -rf ~; fi` (`then`/`do`/`else` are not stripped). All of these were caught by the pre-cycle full-body scan, since the #1245 scrub only applied to a standalone quoted cat. The same-command execution guard _bdb_hd_same_line_exec is then trivially bypassed because it only flags a segment that both names the target basename and has a non-safe-reader command word: `cat x | bash` (cat is a safe reader, the `bash` segment does not name x), `bash x*` (token is `x*`, not `x`), or `bash "$(printf x)"` all pass. Net effect: `cat <<'EOF' > x
$(rm -rf ~)
EOF
cat x | bash` is scrubbed to a header, terminator and `cat x | bash`, so the destructive body never reaches the fence regexes and executes in the same Bash call.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent writes a destructive payload via a 'nonexec' heredoc and executes it in the same command; the guard, which previously scanned the whole body, now allows it silently. Regression of the fence's primary purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: In _bdb_hd_scan_body, run the existing fence regexes over the raw body text in addition to the segment keep-list (i.e. keep the body for regex matching, only drop it for the #1245 standalone-cat special case), or at minimum treat `$(`, backticks, redirect-first words, keywords (then/do/else/elif) and assignment-prefixed `$(` as full-scan triggers regardless of delimiter quoting. In _bdb_hd_same_line_exec, treat any pipeline containing an interpreter/wrapper word (`| bash`, `| sh`, `xargs`) as interpreter-class when any member of that pipeline names the target, and treat tokens containing glob characters or `$`/`\`` as a potential match for the target.

findings.description: The diff introduces `implement_gate.mode: deny`, documented as the only mode in which the gate 'is a fence', and adds a new sanction: a `.run/implement-active.json` marker with `{skill: implement|bug, sprint, started_at}` that unconditionally allows all App Zone writes for two hours. The marker has no integrity protection (no signature, no tie to a harness-controlled signal) and the only control on writing it is the PreToolUse:Write/Edit trust-input ask. The Bash tool is not covered: a single `printf '{"skill":"implement","sprint":"x","started_at":"%s"}' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > .run/implement-active.json` (or running `run-checkpoint.sh mark`) is not blocked by block-destructive-bash.sh and converts deny mode into allow for every subsequent App Zone write. The same holds for forging `state: RUNNING` + fresh `derived_at` in sprint-plan-state.json, but the marker lowers the bar further and is new in this change. The tighten-only claims modifier is also neutralised, since a sanction suppresses the deny branch (line ~595-598).
findings.failure_mode: An agent that wants to write App Zone files outside a run under deny mode forges the marker through Bash and the gate logs `allow / sanctioned_marker` with no ask or deny. The 'fence' provides no enforcement against the only principal it is meant to constrain.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not treat a model-writable file as a sanction under deny mode. Options: have run-checkpoint.sh `mark` write an HMAC over {skill,sprint,started_at} with a key held outside the project tree (e.g. ~/.loa/gate.key, mode 0600) and verify it in check_implement_marker; or require the marker directory to be owned/written only by the harness and add a Bash-side rule in block-destructive-bash.sh that blocks redirects/writes to .run/implement-active.json and the other trust inputs. At minimum document that deny mode is advisory against Bash-capable agents.

findings.description: `LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` in the hook's environment sanctions every App Zone write in every mode with a silent allow. This is the opposite stance from block-destructive-bash.sh in the same diff, which explicitly states 'an environment variable can never switch the fence off'. Hooks inherit the Claude Code process environment, which the agent can influence through the `env` map in `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` (System Zone files that the lead session may write, and which the implement gate does not treat as trust inputs).
findings.failure_mode: An agent adds `"env": {"LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE": "1"}` to settings; from the next session every App Zone write is allowed with only an audit row, defeating deny mode and the claims modifier.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the environment override, or restrict it to ask/telemetry modes so deny can never be loosened by env; if an operator escape hatch is required, read it from a file outside the repository (e.g. ~/.loa/) rather than the process environment, and add `.claude/settings*.json` to the trust-input list so writes to them ask.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml (new) sets guardrails.danger_level.enforce and guardrails.input.enabled to false for both `lean` and `standard`; danger-level-enforcer.sh and input_guardrails.md now resolve those keys through profile-lib.sh with a `false` fallback, so the combined change flips the default and the failure mode.
findings.description: Two security guardrails are turned off by default and made fail-open in one change. (1) `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` previously defaulted to true (`// true`, and `return 0` with no config); `standard` and `lean` profiles now set it false, so an unconfigured or default repository no longer enforces danger levels. (2) `guardrails.input.enabled` (pre-execution prompt guardrails) likewise moves from default-on to default-off in skill-includes/input_guardrails.md. (3) danger-level-enforcer.sh now `source`s profile-lib.sh unguarded at top level and calls `loa_knob ... false`; if the lib is missing, yq is absent, or the config is malformed, the result is empty/false and enforcement is disabled, where previously the yq-failure branch echoed `true`. The orchestrator's documented policy for a non-zero script exit is 'Continue (fail-open)'.
findings.failure_mode: Repositories that relied on danger-level enforcement and input guardrails being on silently lose both after upgrading unless they set the keys or `loa.profile: full` explicitly; tooling errors degrade to no enforcement rather than to the safe default.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the two guardrail keys out of the profile set or set them true in `standard` (treat them as floor keys per floor.yaml), make is_enforcement_enabled return 0 when profile-lib/yq are unavailable (`enforce=$(loa_knob ... true 2>/dev/null) || enforce=true`), and emit a one-time migration WARN when the effective value changes from the pre-cycle default.

findings.description: _bdb_hd_exec_dest decides whether a heredoc write target is 'executable content' and therefore keeps the body under full scan. Its list misses several paths that Claude Code or common tooling execute or load as instructions: `.mcp.json` (MCP server `command`/`args`), `.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/commands/**`, `.claude/agents/**`, `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude/rules/*.md` (prompt surfaces), `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `~/.bash_aliases` (sourced by default Debian/Ubuntu .bashrc but absent from _bdb_hd_re_rc), `.gitattributes`/`.git/info/attributes` (filter/diff drivers), `.github/workflows/*`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.husky/*`, `Makefile`, `package.json` scripts, and `~/.config/systemd/user/*`. Writes to these via `cat <<'EOF' > ...` or `tee` are classified nonexec and their bodies are dropped from the scan.
findings.failure_mode: The documented 'later command' gap widens: a payload planted in one of these files is executed by the harness or a routine tool invocation rather than by an explicit `bash x`, so neither this fence nor the same-line check sees it.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend _bdb_hd_re_sys / _bdb_hd_re_rc with `.mcp.json`, `.claude/(skills|commands|agents|rules)/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.ssh/`, `.bash_aliases`, `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.husky/`, `Makefile`, `package.json`, `.config/systemd/`; or invert the default so that only an explicit allowlist of data-only extensions (.md, .txt, .json outside .claude, .log) is nonexec and everything else keeps the full scan.

findings.cross_file_justification: The deletion in constraints.json propagates to the generated CLAUDE.loa.md Agent Teams table (also removed in this diff) and the truncated files .claude/loa/reference/agent-teams-reference.md and hooks-reference.md, where the enforcing hooks (team-skill-guard.sh, the PreToolUse Write/Edit System Zone guard) are documented.
findings.description: All five agent-teams constraints (C-TEAM-001..005) are deleted, including C-TEAM-005 'teammates MUST NOT modify files in the System Zone (.claude/)… enforced by PreToolUse:Write/Edit hook' (severity critical, incident bridgebuilder-horizon-pr341) and C-TEAM-003/004 (lead-only writes to .run/ state files and git operations). The generated CLAUDE.loa.md section is removed with them, so teammates no longer receive the instruction. Nothing visible in the diff replaces these rules, and the diff also makes `.run/` state files more consequential (SEC-002: they now sanction App Zone writes in deny mode). Whether the mechanical hooks named by the constraints were also removed cannot be confirmed from the shown hunks; the reference docs that would show this were truncated.
findings.failure_mode: If the enforcing hooks were removed or disabled alongside the prose, any teammate can rewrite .claude/ hooks, constraint definitions and .run/ state for the whole team, re-opening the incidents the constraints were created for. Even if hooks remain, removing the prose eliminates the defence-in-depth layer the constraints' `why` fields describe.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm team-skill-guard.sh and the System Zone PreToolUse:Write/Edit guard remain registered for `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` sessions and that tests cover them; if the constraints were consolidated elsewhere, point agent_teams_constraints at the new source rather than deleting them. If agent-teams support is intentionally retired, remove the hook registrations and reference docs in the same change so the state is unambiguous.
